items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: I was privileged to be one of the first white persons to sit in with Joe's band.

ctx.x: At Dreamland. How old were you then? About fourteen, thirteen, about fourteen. Did you know him by this time? Oh, yes. I knew him. You were speaking to him? Oh, yes. Sure. Was he nice to you? Very nice. Very nice. He thought it was wonderful that someone could try to play like him. Did you ever get together with him? Oh, yes. I was privileged to be one of the first white persons to sit in with Joe's band. Oh, yeah? Because he wouldn't let you sit in if you couldn't play. He didn't care who you were. Uh-huh. And…

What's where? You used to write that myth. Well, you used to the only song I know in that band. What band is that? They call it the rhythm case. It's called the rhythm case? Yeah. Myth mode? Yeah. No, myth didn't make it. I'm a myth.

items.title: Muggsy Spanier Interview, 1961-02-02
items.q: Yes, it was because Joe had a distinctive style and he used that mute, you know, and I used that mute. And I just liked his style.

ctx.x: Can you tell us any more about Joe Oliver or anything? What impressed you about his style or was it different than the music around Chicago or something?

Yes, it was because Joe had a distinctive style and he used that mute, you know, and I used that mute. And I just liked his style. It was a swinging lead style. He didn't make a lot of notes or anything like that. He just kept time. He'd just swing the band. He was sort of a feeder, as we call a feeder like I do. I'm a feeder with the band and I just stay around the melody and weave in and out and let the other fellas go ahead.
We enjoyed hearing you play Dipper Mouth last night with your plunger and all. Did Joe ever use the rubber plunger or mostly another kind of a mute?
